entry.title: Slowing Down Time
entry.content:
Last ten years life has been pretty busy. Packed daily schedules with activities planned from the wake of dawn till the crack of the night sky. I have produced great results and achieved very cool things but also it feels like life has just flown by. It feels like my youth years are already up and another few years and I will be looking at old age. I guess there is nothing wrong with life in the fast lane, I definitely prefer this over a boring life where I have no purpose and nothing to do. But it does feel like I have missed the happy moments when they arrived or the good times when I was living them or sitting with the bad times and used them to level up and if only if there was a way to slow life down I cherish these moments more. These days it feels like all feelings happy or sad are very ephemeral and theres always another task to do or a goal to run after and there is no time to sit and feel or to sit and think. And it generally feels like life is slipping by like quick sand in an hour glass. Hours feel like minutes and days feel like hours and there is never enough time.

When we were younger, summer vacations felt like years. We played football till our knees hurt not until the clock turned 7. In college after the classes, we walked around until we were too hungry or it was too dark. Days were long and semesters were longer. So in an effort to feel again and escape the clockwork every so once in a while, something that I have started doing is journaling once a week where I just look back on my week and also think about what lies ahead in the week after. Its a really good pause to reflect and plan and greatly helps absorb what really happened in the week before. I also really like to abstain from my routine on Sundays to give my brain a little bit of change. So other than a couple of chores I welcome new plans and activities on Sundays. Those catch ups or spontaneous drives, all are very attractive.

Growing up I also never really understood why my parents never wanted to do anything on vacations. I was very puzzled why they would travel all this way to just sleep or aimlessly walk around. Now I know for them it was just a way to escape the routine. Escape the time compression. For them planning out activities and being “busy” on the vacation really beat the purpose of the vacation. And I do see now how vacations out of your routine can help slow time down as long as you dont get carried away with the pressure of sight seeing or doing something all the time. So now I believe in a healthy balance of activities and just not doing anything while on vacations as the best policy.

Another thing that helps slow time down is trying something new. When you do something new your brain gets kicked out of the autopilot and becomes fully conscious to understand and learn the new activity. I have recently tried padel, flying a drone, trying korean barbecue and all of them helped slow time down and helped me be in the moment. Its really hard to be in the moment in the activities I do everyday like driving or cooking breakfast or working out in the gym. Although ideally I am able to be fully focussed and in the moment even during those activities since it conserves energy and also increases the quality of that task. This part is work in progress!
entry.summary: You blink and life just passes by?

entry.title: Working Towards an Opportunity Level Harry Kane

link.title: Working Towards an Opportunity Level Harry Kane

entry.content:
Its the Ballon D’or 2026 week and the fresh news is that an English Player is the 2026 Mens Ballon D’or Winner. Harry Kane did it! Whoever watches football knows that Harry’s journey to this day has been one of the most extra ordinary stories in football. From being rejected from the Arsenal academy to then joining the Tottenham Academy. Then being loaned to several other clubs before finally being a mainstay in the Tottenham first team. Which finally culminated in a blockbuster move to Bayern Munich. Harry Kane has done it all. Harry Kane put in top drawer performances for years in a Tottenham jersey but it was never the place which could bring him any recognition. There is no individual glory in football without team success. But those years of working on his finishing and playmaking, earned him the well deserved move to a team which does and is expected to win many trophies. Bayern Munich wanted and knew what they were getting in Harry Kane, a proven striker with clinical finishing and that they got. But the journey to that point was anything but linear.

Harry Kane knows what it takes to work on yourself and put in consistent performances year after year and work towards a big opportunity. Sometimes opportunities do just present themselves but they are of no use if you arent ready for them. But more often than not as in the case of Harry Kane, you dont just fall into an opportunity, you work towards it. By consistent performances and an undeniable track record you can not only attact opportunities but also produce opportunities for yourself out of thin air. The converse if also equally true. If your reputation is bad and you are inconsistent and havent worked on yourself, opportunities will actively avoid you and get repelled by you.

So lets say your goal is to be the best in the world at something like Harry Kane. What do you do? You deliver consistent performances year after year. You work on yourself, identify your weaknesses work on them, get better. As long as you are getting better and your results (projects in my case) are improving in quality, the lack of success shouldnt let it discourage you. And then inevitably after a certain threshold, with some luck that big opportunity will definitely come knocking your way and when it does, you know you have worked towards that opportunity. You know you ready to smash that opportunity so then dont wait until you be the best in the world.
entry.summary: Does an opportunity just present itself or do you work towards it?

entry.title: Pulling the Figurative Andon Cord
entry.content:
So the Andon Cord is a vital part of the Toyota Production System (TPS). From what I remember correctly an Andon Cord is a physical switch you can pull whenever there is a problem on the assembly line which stops the whole assembly line and alerts the Managers about the problem. There are several benefits for doing this. Toyota believes in finding a problem as soon as possible which means not passing on the problem to the next station where it could possibly escalate into something more serious or harder to fix or detect. Pulling the andon cord and stopping the assembly line there and then allows this to happen. Another is kaizen or continuous improvement. Stopping the assembly line sure causes a loss in productivity in the short term but in the long term root causing the problem and fixing it is way better for productivity than hiding problems under the carpet until they build up and cause a catastropic failure. I also read somewhere that Toyota measured the health of a factory by the number of Andon Cord Pulls. If there were none thats suspicious because there is no way there are zero problems in the whole factory which meant the factory was hiding problems which is a serious quality and safety issue.

When I worked at Woven by Toyota even though we didnt have any assembly line we sure were still making software products and passing them onto someone else to use downstream. We had a company wide “Andon Cord” policy where anyone could pull a digital andon card if they sense a safety risk in any part of the software. In our simulator team also we practiced this philosophy strongly. If you see something off, raise it, create a ticket or slack post, get some eyes on it dont just ignore it and forget about it. With Murphys law, if that was actually a bug it is likely bug about again and next time it might have a much worse timing.

We can practice pulling a figurative Andon Cord on the personal level too. If at work or elsewhere, if you see something off definitely raise it. If you see something unsafe definitely report it to the right authorities. If you see unprofessional behavior from a co worker, communicate it to the HR. You owe to your own safety and also the well being of those around you to always equip yourself with an Andon Cord and use it responsibly.
entry.summary: Speaking up if you see a problem

entry.title: Avoiding the Checklist Mindset
entry.content:
The checklist mindset is when you make a checklist of all your open tasks and then race through the checklist with the intention of just finishing the checklist with no actual concern for how well you are doing the tasks or how important is one task over another.

The checklist mindset at face value is really good at getting tasks “done”. But thats not the only important thing is there? Some tasks are long running tasks which need planning or more careful consideration. Some tasks are risky and could lead to more tasks if not done well. Some tasks have higher stakes, where failure is not an option or where people’s emotions are involved and someone could get hurt. Not all tasks are as simple as “Buy milk from the grocery store”. Some are more nuanced and the checklist mindset does not account for that at all.

So what is the checklist mindset good at? The checklist mindset is really good at defining all the tasks and getting you started on the tasks. It reduces the activation energy / inertia and puts you into motion which is usually half the work done but not always.

So how can we improve on / fix the checklist mindset. The focus needs to shift from “finishing all the tasks” to “doing all the tasks well”. Some augmentations can be added. First is once the checklist is ready do a second pass on the checklist and bump the important tasks to the top of the list. Do the important high stakes tasks first. Like the famous saying “Swallow the frog”.

The second augmentation that can be added is while starting on a task, before proceeding with the first action that comes to your mind, ask yourself what are the risks involved? Is there a better way of doing this task? Am I rushing the task or can it wait? How much does quality matter in this task? If the answer to this question is yes then abstain on the task, bump it to the bottom of the list and get back to it at a later time when you have more mental bandwidth for it.

An example I can think of where the checklist mindset completely ruined the task was when a friend of mine has asked me to intervene in their relationship so my job was to call his/her partner and try and clarify something. I wasnt able to find time do this and suddenly I found myself with a few minutes waiting for another friend to arrive at the restaurant. Checklist mindset kicked in. Was their risk involved? Yes. Was their a possibility of someone getting hurt? Yes. Is quality important in this task? Extremely. Inspite of this I decided to sneak in this task before my friend arrived. The call went horribly. The network connection was poor so we couldnt hear each other properly. I was only half attentive because I was also waiting for that other friend at the restaurant. There was a lot of ambient noise which made it harder to talk. I had not really gathered my thoughts properly because I was context switching. Literally nothing went well on the call and I just came off as insensitive and immature. And was the task done? Absolutely not, it actually led to more tasks. So yeah with the second augmentation from before, I should have absolutely abstained on the task and waited for much a better time and place to do it.

So in summary the way to escape the checklist mindset is by recognising not all tasks have equal importance, some tasks need quality more than other tasks do and then rearranging the order of the tasks so that tasks get done but they also get done WELL!
entry.summary: Differentiating between your buying milk from the grocery store and hanging out with your girlfriend

entry.title: The 5 minute rule
entry.content:
So I am a TO-DO list person. Whenever I think of a task that needs to be done I add it to my TO-DO list. I have been using Asana in which you can classify the tasks into multiple lists based on importance or urgency but honestly all tasks end up in the same list. It is hard to stay organized on that. Now TO-DO lists become this massive dump yard if they are not cleaned once in a while. My usually policy is to clean them once a week but my TO-DO list is always overflowing and the promised glory day when I reach zero tasks on the list remains a pipe dream.

So something thats worked very effectively for me to keep the dumy yard relatively small is the 5 minute rule. If a new tasks comes up then ask yourself, will this take less than 5 minutes of my time? If yes just try to do it then and there and get over with it. If not then yes it can find a place on your TO-DO list.

Its a deceptively simple productivity hack but it is extremely effective. Conquer your tasks 5 minutes at a time.

entry.title: Return To India
entry.content:
So I moved back to India after five years in the US. After a lot of deliberation I decided that for my personal life and career India is the better option. Yes thats the truth.

Getting back to life on the India’s roads has been somewhat amusing. So the other day I was driving my car and I saw this person lets call him RakeshJi trying to cross the road on a zebra crossing while I was turning onto the road. Now its very ingrained in me that I will stop and let him cross. But Rakeshji gave me this confused look and he has no idea why I am stopping in the middle of the road. So he decides to walk towards my car, give me a very puzzled look and then walk around my car. And while this is happening everyone behind me is honking. One guy on a two wheeler even came next to my window and asked, “Bro are you sleeping?”. Noone in that 5 mile radius thought I was sane.

Something similar happened the other day when I was going to Deccan gymkhana. The road has no sidewalk and so the pedestrians were walking on the road, I mean where else would they walk right? So I started driving on pedestrian speed and then everyone behind me just started honking. And I am like either the pedestrians need to get wings and disappear from the road or we reach a few minutes late if we want to use this road. I sense not many people agree with me on the latter option. It would be kinda cool if pedestrians start carrying around tiny horns in their hands so that they can honk back. Because without that it sounds like a pretty unequal battle. Let the honk battle begin!

Now consider this intersection that I encounter everyday on my way home from work. There are no signals at this intersection so its largely an intersection left to be overseen by Gods. Theres always a traffic jam at this intersection. So I found myself asking why we dont why Stop signs in India which work so beautifully in the US. For those of you who dont know what Stop signs are, they mean stop at intersection and allow whoever reached first to go first and if everyone follows that traffic flows like water. Until one day I saw that, this intersection did indeed have a stop sign. But only facing one direction. What is the point of a stop sign which only tells one side of the intersection to stop for others but everyone else have no rules. So the stop sign is mostly for aesthetics. Because aesthetics are important. Because a road should look like road right. So lets put up some signs and mark some lanes and then we’ll forget about them.

The other day I was going to work in the morning and there was this guy on a floating sofa coming towards me really fast. So I slowed down then he came closer and I saw the faint outline of a two wheeler on the couch. Then he came even closer and it was actually a whole three seater sofa on a two wheeler. Whoever said you need a UHaul truck to transport a sofa? You just need a two wheeler.

And then has anyone seen the BMW or Mercedes Benz auto rickshaws? With those big logos at the back? Its really cool to see the big automotive companies leaving F1 and entering the rickshaw market. They have finally realised how lucrative and on brand the rickshaw market can be in India.

Recently I also had to go to Mumbai late at night to catch a flight to my friends wedding and the highway traffic was another beast. So the fastest lane had the slowest cars. Think a truck or a dumper. Some trucks have blow horn written at the back, some trucks have horn not okay please and sometimes both are written right next to each other. Then there was also a bus swerving through the traffic increasing everyones anxiety. Then a truck with no lights at the back so it was almost invisible until you got real close to it and realised it had lights on the sides but not on the back.

To add to all this it was raining very heavily so everyone had hazard lights on. So since the turn indicators were out of action you were playing the guessing game of whos going to turn and when. Okay fine still doable since you were being extra extra careful. Then in all this, a red inter state bus in front of us who did not have the hazard lights on, turned right with the left indicator. Okay so apart from the turning guessing game, theres also a turning lying game also going on. If this was a video game it would be the advanced extra hard legendary boss level.

After moving back I decided to live independently instead of crashing with my parents, so I started looking for houses. It was really funny to see my dad explain it to his friends about this. He went something like “Neel wants to contemplate so he will stay away only for one year”. I wasnt sure if I should laugh or cry?

So I got introduced to a broker through my friend and he asked me, “What are your requirements?”. I was like I want an apartment with a dishwasher. He said, “Yeah we have dishwashers, they are called maids / mavshi”. Then I said, “No, no I want an automated dishwasher like a washing machine that I can use myself”. He said, “Next requirement?”

I told him, “I want a house close to the grocery store”. He said, “Why? Just use an app for groceries or just tell the mavshi dont get anything oily, which vegetables you dont like and she will pick it up from the grocery store.” So basically getting a mavshi is a lot like getting a Claude code or ChatGPT subscription. If you let go of a little control and prompt it the right way, prompts go in and food comes out.

entry.title: Is he going to play every point like that?

link.title: Is he going to play every point like that?

entry.content:
My favourite ad of all time is Rafa Nadal’s Nike ad where they show glimpses of Nadal’s entire career cut as a single point of a tennis match. Nadal covers every inch of the tennis court on different surfaces, in different competitions against different players and then ends up winning the point. And then the commentator goes “Wow, this guy is relentless, is he going to play every point like that?”.

Its a rhetorical question of course, Nadal did play every point across his entire career like that. Like it was his last point. Like his life depended on it. Would Nadal have achieved everything he achieved without doing that? Probably not. How important was this in everything he achieved? Definitely atleast makes the top three factors.

A lot of people are talented and have the potential to do great things. But very few people actually become a Nadal. In my opinion the difference is this: relentless consistency. Waking up every day and giving your best. Not settling for anything else. This shit is hard. And its probably because of multiple reasons. One is maybe not even recognising your talent and potential. If one doesnt even think they have the potential to become special then they are probably not going to put in the insane amount of hard work needed to nurture it. The other is that achieving greatness is super hard and there are way easier distractions all around you all the fucking time. So you got to want it really bad for some really strong reason so that you can say no to the other distractions.

So how do you achieve relentless consistency? Exposure to hard work and a strong work ethic and its benefits during your childhood definitely helps. Moreover a strong belief in self improvement through hardwork. Believing that you can always one up yourself. Beat your PR. Raise the bar for yourself. And doing that again and again and again. Eventually that becomes second nature. Actually doing something you love helps too. If you get no joy from what you are doing, obviously achieving relentless consistency becomes difficult. Someone who believes in your potential to achieve great things is important too. As a child its hard to bet on yourself, but if there is a third figure who does that becomes a game changer. And then if you embrace this process, enjoy your day to day and achieve relentless consistency then a side product is achieving greatness like Nadal did.

entry.title: Team player level Ted Lasso
entry.content:
Ted Lasso is hired into english football as a coach with the only thing riding on his side is his ability to work with people and an optimistic leadership style. And as it turns out these qualities are extremely effective in a team sport like football.

My favourite dynamic in the series is Ted Lasso and the club kitman Nathan Shelley. Nathan Shelley has no formal training in football but like most football fans has very strong (and useful) opinions about his team. Ted who happens to be a bit of a beginner in football himself values useful opinions from anywhere and everywhere. Doesnt matter where they come from. The guy is a learning machine and willing to learn from anyone and anyhow. For a newly hired coach to be open to learning from the the kitman, he has to have absolutely no ego, just an ability to consider any and all suggestions objectively.

Ted lasso understands his role really well which is to make sure his club is successful. Hes not hired to prove that his is the best manager in the world or that is he a great coach, etc.. All he cares about is the team above all. He has zero credit seeking inclinations, he just does his job well and moves on with his life.

My favourite scene in the series is Nate’s locker room roast. Nathon writes down some harsh honest thoughts about each player on the team and passes them to Ted. Ted in classic style isnt thinking about who delivers the message to the players. He only cares about whos best qualified or who will be the most effective in delivering the message to the players. Ted believes that Nate has the credibility and insight to deliver the message effectively. So to Nathan’s surprise, Ted asks him to deliver his thoughts which he obviously nails and AFC Richmond win their next game. Ted did what a real team player would do which is recognize and empower other people’s strengths.

Ted makes all this look very easy but hes mastered some fundamental qualities to do this. Letting go of any ego. Focusing on getting the job done over personal accolades and credit. Being will to learn from anyone, regardless of the credit. Thinking of oneself as just a medium to do the work. Always putting the team above yourself. Separating the ownership of the outcome from the ownership of the credit.

Ultimately being a team player is not about making yourself smaller its about making your team bigger. Dont prove that you are the smartest, prove that the smartest ideas can win.
entry.summary: Work for the team before you work for yourself

entry.title: Host Everything
entry.content:
Hosting everything is about taking control of your life. Expressing your personality and character. Asking the questions what do I want from this? What would I like to do? What do I want from life? And then actually making it happen.

When I was younger I was too busy trying to “fit in”. In the recent years I have realised a way more sustainable way to live is to just be yourself and where you fit tends to automatically find you. Hosting everything is about just bringing yourself into all situations. Instead of waiting for the answers, trying to answer the questions yourself. Even if they sometimes miss the mark. Instead of waiting for someone else to tell you what to do, getting into the habit of asking yourself within what you want to do and then expressing it.

I have experienced that hosting everything you tend to enjoy the outcome way more than otherwise and believe it or not it also increases your value in your group because suddenly you are the one contributing ideas and setting the direction which is admittedly one of the hardest things to do. So whenever in doubt, just assume you are hosting. Going to a meeting and not sure what the agenda is? Prepare before hand and go with an agenda prepared. A dinner plan is brewing but logistics are still up in the air? Propose a time and place that you think would be a good fit.

What starts to happen is when you start hosting these small things in life, it slowly also prepares you to host the big decisions in life. Where do I want to live? What career do I want? Who do I want to marry? If you dont practice hosting the small decisions you will never have the muscle ready to host the big ones! Just following conventional wisdom is probably the worst thing you can do for yourself.

Also hosting everything does not mean just dominate everyone else. It just means having a plan ready but also being open to a change of plan if something better comes up. This is also in line with what the science of Imrprov tells you. While doing improv you should have strong opinions about the character and the scene you are in. But if your scene partner throws another idea, you quickly “Yes, AND?” to jump on a new reality instead. So always try to define your reality but be receptive to gifts from others. Host everything!
entry.summary: Become the captain of your own ship

entry.title: Another Fucking Opportunity for Growth
entry.content:
This is one of those things that I have always done fairly well but until I read it in book (Connect), I didnt really know what I was doing. Celebrating failures. Trying hard things despite high risk of failure. Being suspicous about yourself if you havent really failed at anything for a really long time. All these things are very counter intuitive. Why would you celebrate your own failures? Why would you go looking for failures?

It turns out when you start accepting failures as a part of the process. As stepping stones to success thats truly when you start winning. The winners and champions, they know that failure isnt the end of the road. Its just an AFOG: Another fucking opportunity for growth. Its like life telling them that they arent ready yet, here are things that they need to do better and try again. So when you start treating failures as AFOG, you actually start listening. You get better. You get stronger. Like that classic line experience or failures are the best teacher.

Nothing ever worth achieving was achieved without a ton of failures along the way. Then why are you so entitled that you think you can achieve those things without any failures? What doesnt kill you should and will make you stronger. A strong corollary is that if you havent failed in a while that usually means you stopped trying. You arent pushing yourself hard enough. And you can do way better. And then when you arent afraid of failing, something magical happens. You arent afraid of taking risks. You arent afraid of the hard things. You push yourself out of the comfort zone. And that starts a very self reinforcing cycle of growth. Where you will eventually be capable of doing things you could never dream of. Of taking on things that were well beyond your horizon. And that sounds like a life worth living.
